patents.source: USPTO Open Data Portal, granted patents since 2001, applicant phrase "cognizant", 2026-10-06

reading.body:
Cognizant holds 169 granted patents, and its five most recent are all AI or cloud automation tooling, granted between March and June 2026.

The recent titles cluster around automating work that used to require human judgment: data analytics, cloud deployment configuration, prescriptors, application modernization sequencing, and parametric activation functions. That is the shape of a services firm converting delivery know-how into patented methods, not a chipmaker or model lab building frontier systems. The patents are process claims, which means Cognizant's AI position rests on how work gets done rather than on compute it owns.

For AI scaling, this matters as a demand signal rather than a supply one. Firms that automate cloud deployment and application modernization are the ones moving enterprise workloads onto infrastructure, and that migration is what pulls power. The data does not show Cognizant's data centers, its power contracts, or its compute footprint, so nothing here speaks to the grid constraint directly. It also does not show revenue, headcount, or whether these patents are licensed or defensive.

The profile text adds a claimed study of 10,000-plus workers and $6 trillion in trapped productivity, but that is Cognizant's own framing, not an independent measurement. The patent record is the harder fact: 169 grants since 2001, with the newest batch dated 2026. What the data cannot say is whether any of these methods ship in products customers pay for.

profile_text.body:
Cognizant is a public company, traded under the ticker CTSH, that presents itself as an AI builder. Its site states that "the most impactful AI isn't bought - it's built," and the company says it bridges the gap between the AI that is available and the AI a business needs. It cites agentic AI and context engineering among the emerging trends and technologies it covers in its podcasts.

The site also references a global study of 10,000-plus workers that Cognizant says reveals hidden segments in the workforce and $6 trillion in trapped productivity behind an AI adoption gap. The company is registered with the SEC under CIK 0001058290.
